markets: Sells door hardware, electronic access and hotel locks across Europe, North America, Asia-Pacific and the Middle East.
rationale: Hospitality-focused access brand with global customers; B2B hotel and venue relevance, though mostly industrial marketing.
changed: Formed in 2015 by merger of Dorma and Kaba

name: Transinfo Group
desc: Chinese provider of intelligent transportation systems, urban rail and public transport data, software and solutions.
markets: Public transport and rail customers in China, judged from its profile; international activity not confirmed.
rationale: Government-facing transport technology firm with little brand marketing and a China focus; weak F1 fit.

name: United Internet
desc: German internet services group, founded in 1988, whose brands include 1&1, IONOS, GMX and web.de for hosting, mobile and email.
markets: Customers across Germany, Europe and the United States, including IONOS web hosting; founder Ralph Dommermuth is largest shareholder.
rationale: Consumer and business internet brands with European reach; German market presence and hospitality for hosting clients could suit F1.

name: Actifio
desc: Former US data management company whose copy data management platform let enterprises back up, recover and reuse data across clouds.
markets: Enterprise customers worldwide; acquired by Google in December 2020 and folded into Google Cloud.
rationale: Brand absorbed into Google Cloud; parent Google is already a current F1 partner.
changed: Acquired by Google in 2020
f1: Parent Google is a current F1 partner

name: Apttus
desc: Former US software company selling cloud applications for configure-price-quote, contract management and revenue lifecycle processes.
markets: Enterprise customers worldwide; merged with Conga and rebranded Conga in 2020, owned by Thoma Bravo.
rationale: Brand no longer exists; successor Conga is not an F1 partner, and the name has been retired.
changed: Merged with Conga and rebranded Conga in 2020

name: Dotc United Group
desc: Chinese internet technology company that builds internet platforms and cloud services under the DotC United brand, covering mobile services.
markets: Based in Shanghai, China; customers and international operations not confirmed.
rationale: Little confirmed information; Chinese internet firm with an unclear business, so no specific F1 case.

name: GLG
desc: Expert network founded in 1998 by Mark and Thomas Gerson, connecting investors, consultants and corporations with industry experts for advice.
markets: Clients including investors and corporations across North America, Europe and Asia.
rationale: B2B research brand with financial and corporate clients; hospitality could suit client entertainment, though marketing is discreet.

name: iFlytek
desc: Chinese AI company, founded in 1999 as a University of Science and Technology of China spin-off, making speech AI.
markets: Sells speech recognition, education and translation products mainly in China, with some international sales.
rationale: Chinese AI group with speech technology; sanctions-related scrutiny and domestic focus reduce F1 fit despite its technology profile.

name: Marigold
desc: Marketing technology company formed in 2021 from Campaign Monitor, Cheetah Digital, Sailthru and others, offering email and customer engagement tools.
markets: Customers in North America, Europe and Australia through Campaign Monitor and related brands.
rationale: Marketing software brand with international clients; B2B hospitality could suit, but marketing spend is modest.
changed: Formed in 2021 by combining Campaign Monitor, Cheetah Digital and Sailthru

name: Verafin
desc: Canadian financial crime management software company whose cloud platform detects fraud and money laundering for banks and credit unions.
markets: Customers are banks and credit unions mainly in the US and Canada; acquired by Nasdaq in 2021.
rationale: Owned by Nasdaq, a current F1 partner, so any activity would run through the parent.
changed: Acquired by Nasdaq in 2021
f1: Parent Nasdaq is a current F1 partner

name: vXchnge
desc: Former US data centre colocation provider operating edge data centres in regional markets such as Boston, Dallas, Philadelphia and Raleigh.
markets: Edge data centres in US regional markets only; current ownership and status not confirmed.
rationale: Regional US colocation firm with little marketing activity and unclear current status; weak F1 fit.

name: Algolia
desc: Search and discovery platform providing a hosted API for site search and recommendations, founded in 2012 in Paris.
markets: Customers across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific; founded in France in 2012.
rationale: Developer-focused brand with global e-commerce clients; hospitality and technology showcase feasible, with French and US roots.

name: Amplitude
desc: Digital analytics company whose product analytics platform lets product, marketing and engineering teams track user behaviour, founded in 2012.
markets: Customers across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific; listed through a direct listing in 2021.
rationale: Data-analytics brand with an obvious real-time data theme; F1 has analytics partners, though marketing budget is moderate.

name: Contentful
desc: Software company selling a composable content platform, a headless content management system, with a large presence in San Francisco.
markets: Enterprise customers across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific; offices in Berlin and San Francisco.
rationale: Enterprise software brand with global customers; F1 already has several software partners, and hospitality suits enterprise sales.

name: Infinidat
desc: Enterprise data storage company, founded in 2011 by Moshe Yanai, selling InfiniBox and InfiniGuard storage systems to large organisations.
markets: Customers in North America, Europe and Asia; large R&D centre in Israel.
rationale: Enterprise storage vendor where F1 partners such as NetApp already compete; hospitality useful for large clients.

name: Iterable
desc: Cross-channel marketing automation platform used by brands to send personalised email, push, SMS and in-app messages with AI.
markets: Customers in North America and Europe, among consumer brands; no specific expansion plans known.
rationale: Marketing-technology brand with consumer-brand customers; B2B hospitality could suit, but marketing budget is moderate.

name: Jamf
desc: Software company making tools to manage, secure and deploy Apple devices like Macs and iPhones in schools and businesses.
markets: Customers in North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific; agreed in 2025 to be taken private by Francisco Partners.
rationale: Established enterprise software brand with global customers; technology showcase and hospitality fit, though marketing budget is moderate.
changed: Agreed to be taken private by Francisco Partners in 2025

name: LaunchDarkly
desc: Feature management platform that lets engineering teams release, toggle and test software features safely without redeploying code.
markets: Customers in North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific; no specific expansion plans known.
rationale: Developer-tooling brand with real-time release control; technology tie-in exists, but marketing budget is moderate.

name: Molo Finance
desc: Digital mortgage platform that helps UK homebuyers and borrowers apply for mortgages faster, mixing automated underwriting with human support.
markets: UK homebuyers and borrowers, judged from its London base; no international activity known.
rationale: UK-only mortgage start-up with limited budget; British Grand Prix gives reach but fit is weak.

name: Oosto
desc: Israeli computer vision company, formerly AnyVision, offering facial recognition and object recognition software for security and access control.
markets: Israeli development with enterprise and government customers in several regions; US head office shown by Crunchbase.
rationale: Facial recognition vendor with sensitive reputation and modest marketing; weak F1 fit.
changed: Renamed from AnyVision to Oosto in 2021

name: PatSnap
desc: Intellectual property and innovation intelligence software company, founded in China in 2007, operating from Singapore with offices in Shenzhen.
markets: Corporate and research customers in Asia, North America and Europe; offices in several regions.
rationale: Innovation analytics brand with global customers; Singapore Grand Prix hospitality could suit, though marketing budget is moderate.

name: Qumulo
desc: Enterprise file storage software company, founded in 2012, whose scale-out file data platform runs on-premises and in public clouds.
markets: Customers in media, healthcare and research in North America, Europe and Asia; no specific expansion plans known.
rationale: Storage software vendor with data-heavy customers; F1 already has storage partners, and hospitality could suit enterprise sales.

name: Redis
desc: Data technology company that commercialises the open-source Redis in-memory database, used for caching, real-time data and AI applications.
markets: Developers and enterprises worldwide use Redis; offices across North America, Europe and Asia.
rationale: Real-time data brand with developer reach; technology showcase fit with F1 telemetry, and enterprise hospitality possible.

name: SnapLogic
desc: Enterprise software company, founded in 2006 by Gaurav Dhillon, whose integration platform as a service connects business applications and data.
markets: Enterprise customers in North America, Europe and Asia; no specific expansion plans known.
rationale: Enterprise integration vendor with B2B hospitality value, but modest brand marketing and small scale.

name: Unqork
desc: No-code enterprise application platform, founded in 2017 by Gary Hoberman, letting banks, insurers and governments build complex software without code.
markets: Customers are banks, insurers and governments, mainly in the United States; no verified wider expansion.
rationale: Enterprise no-code vendor with US financial clients; hospitality could suit, but a limited consumer brand.

name: Vectra AI
desc: Cybersecurity company, founded in 2011, whose platform uses AI to detect and prioritise attacks across networks, cloud and identity.
markets: Enterprise customers across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific; no specific expansion plans known.
rationale: Cybersecurity brand with enterprise clients; F1 has several security partners, so hospitality and technology showcase are plausible.

name: Workfront
desc: Former enterprise work management software company whose cloud platform helped marketing and creative teams plan projects; now part of Adobe.
markets: Enterprise customers worldwide; acquired by Adobe in December 2020 and folded into Adobe Experience Cloud.
rationale: Brand absorbed into Adobe, a current F1 partner, so any activity would run through the parent.
changed: Acquired by Adobe in 2020
f1: Parent Adobe is a current F1 partner
